minutes.headline: Override failed; committee accepts a balanced-budget of cuts and eyes another override attempt next year
minutes.summary: The committee processed the fallout of the failed override, with the superintendent outlining the resulting cuts (class sizes, interventionists, middle school sports and transportation, high school world language) and recommending the district implement the balanced budget and form a community task force rather than return to voters immediately. The committee elected new officers for 2026-2027 -- Laura as chair, Tony as vice chair, Mandy Gilman provisionally as secretary -- adopted several revised policies (cash handling, student data privacy, medication administration, advertising), tabled the fifth-grade bus-release procedure pending community feedback, and voted a composite evaluation of the superintendent's first year.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the committee and staff for their override effort despite its failure, and welcomed the idea of community reading volunteers in the lower grades.
Thanked the committee for its work through budget season, and recounted a years-old effort with other parents to change the fourth/fifth-grade bus release rule.
Asked about legal options for raising money to restore the cut middle school sports budget, and what options exist for a student whose sport (golf, ski, lacrosse) is no longer offered.
Thanked the superintendent for her visibility at school events, and raised the status of the ski team's co-op arrangement and the golf team cut.

budget_items.what_was_said: A committee member said the Senate had put more money in the budget for Lunenburg, calling it a significant amount, but cautioned the district would not know for certain until July and does not budget on that money.
A commission to review the state education funding formula is included in the Senate budget; if it advances, its report would not be due until fall 2028, meaning any resulting funding is years away.
The committee authorized student activity fund amounts for each school for the coming year.
The business office reported there were no line item transfers to review this week.
Several scholarship donations were in the committee's packet for acceptance, some to be dispersed directly to students and others accepted on students' behalf without naming recipients.
The policy caps cash accepted for a single school transaction, a figure described as a compromise reached after feedback from teachers who wanted to keep small cash activities like coin-counting.

budget_items.topic: Cash cap vs. prom ticket pricing
budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked whether the cash cap should be raised to cover prom ticket sales; the superintendent argued for keeping the cap and reassessing after a year rather than repeatedly adjusting it, and noted an electronic-payment service fee per transaction.
A resident said the entire prior year's middle school sports budget being eliminated was just under a stated figure, and asked what legal options exist to raise money to restore it.

transfers.description: line item transfers for the week

decisions.decision: The outgoing chair announced he will not continue as chair and will nominate Laura as his successor.
The committee expressed general support for implementing the balanced budget (option three) and possibly forming a community task force, without taking a formal vote that night.

The fifth-grade bus-release question was treated as a procedure under the superintendent's authority rather than school committee policy; the superintendent will gather community feedback and report back.
Formal approval to train non-medical staff in nasal naloxone administration was deferred until a written procedure is developed.

what_happened.line: After the override failed, the committee leaned toward implementing a balanced budget built on cuts to class sizes, interventionists, middle school sports and transportation, and high school world language, rather than returning to voters right away.
The committee elected Laura as chair and Tony as vice chair for 2026-2027, with Mandy Gilman named secretary pending her acceptance.
The fifth-grade bus-release procedure was tabled so the superintendent can gather community feedback before any change.
The committee adopted revised policies on cash handling, student data privacy, medication administration, and advertising in schools.
The committee accepted a composite evaluation of the superintendent's first year.

why_it_matters: The override's failure is now translating into specific reductions -- class sizes, interventionist staffing, middle school sports and transportation, and a high school language program -- while the committee weighs a community task force before deciding whether to ask voters again.
The new cash-handling policy sets a cap on cash accepted per school transaction, which came up directly in connection with how prom tickets can be sold going forward.

Families with fourth- and fifth-graders should watch for the superintendent's community feedback process on bus release, since it is being handled as an administrative procedure rather than a committee policy vote.
watch_next: The superintendent's report back on fifth-grade bus-release community feedback
Any future override vote or the community task force's recommendations

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on every routine vote (scholarships, policy re-adoptions, student activity accounts, auditorium waiver, reorganization, all four third-read policies, superintendent evaluation) and on the transfer/warrant line, with only name-spelling caption errors on our side. The real gaps are: a grants-authorization vote and a naloxone-training deferral that appear only in our minutes with no official record at all, a fifth-grade bus-release outcome that the two records describe completely differently (procedural referral vs. simply "tabled"), and an internal contradiction in the official minutes naming the already-elected chair as the secretary nominee instead of Gilman.
